content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To play the trombone, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Apply slide lubricant to the inner slide (2 minutes)
Step 2. Research different trombone brands (2 days)
Step 3. Purchase a beginner tenor trombone (3 hours)
Step 4. Buy a sturdy music stand (15 minutes)
Step 5. Perform a basic C major scale (1 minute)
Step 6. Practice buzzing with just the mouthpiece (10 minutes)
Step 7. Learn to hold the instrument with correct posture (15 minutes)
Step 8. Watch a video on trombone maintenance (20 minutes)
Step 9. Clean the mouthpiece with warm soapy water (5 minutes)
Step 10. Label the seven slide positions on a chart (30 minutes)
Step 11. Practice the transition from 1st to 4th position (20 minutes)
Step 12. Set up a dedicated practice space (1 hour)
Step 13. Purchase a mouthpiece brush and cleaning snake (15 minutes)
Step 14. Download a metronome app (2 minutes)
Step 15. Play a long tone on Bb2 (30 seconds)
Step 16. Study a diagram of the trombone's parts (10 minutes)
Step 17. Buy a comfortable chair for playing (45 minutes)
Step 18. Learn how to read bass clef notation (1 week)
Step 19. Find a local trombone instructor (3 days)
Step 20. Wipe down the outer slide with a microfiber cloth (3 minutes)
Step 21. Practice diaphragmatic breathing exercises (15 minutes)
Step 22. Memorize the slide position for Eb (10 minutes)
Step 23. Rent a trombone from a music shop (1 hour)
Step 24. Learn the slide position for F (5 minutes)
Step 25. Order a beginner's method book (15 minutes)
Step 26. Assemble the bell section and slide section (1 minute)
Step 27. Schedule a first introductory lesson (15 minutes)
Step 28. Play a simple folk melody (2 minutes)
Step 29. Unpack the trombone from its case (2 minutes)
Step 30. Study the overtone series for trombone (2 hours)
Step 31. Visit a music conservatory gallery (4 hours)
Step 32. Attend a live brass quintet performance (2 hours)
Step 33. Place sheet music on the stand (10 seconds)
Step 34. Find a fingering and slide chart online (5 minutes)
Step 35. Insert the mouthpiece into the leadpipe (5 seconds)
Step 36. Buy a bottle of slide oil (10 minutes)
Step 37. Learn the harmonic series on Bb (30 minutes)
Step 38. Practice finding 3rd position accurately (15 minutes)
Step 39. Listen to a recording of JJ Johnson (1 hour)
Step 40. Apply tuning slide grease (5 minutes)
Step 41. Read the "Introduction to Brass" chapter (40 minutes)
Step 42. Warm up your facial muscles (2 minutes)
Step 43. Practice tonguing techniques (20 minutes)
Step 44. Watch a masterclass on YouTube (1 hour)
Step 45. Search for "how to play trombone" tutorials (10 minutes)
Step 46. Buy a digital chromatic tuner (20 minutes)
Step 47. Check the water key for proper seal (1 minute)
Step 48. Practice a slow legato slide movement (10 minutes)
Step 49. Brush your teeth before playing (3 minutes)
Step 50. Look up the history of the sackbut (1 hour)
Step 51. Learn the slide position for D (5 minutes)
Step 52. Check the tension of the slide lock (30 seconds)
Step 53. Play a low Bb note (10 seconds)
Step 54. Go to a local music store (30 minutes)
Step 55. Secure the slide cream lid (30 seconds)
Step 56. Tighten the bell lock nut (30 seconds)
Step 57. Practice buzzing into a leadpipe (5 minutes)
Step 58. Clear a spot on the floor for the case (5 minutes)
Step 59. Sit down in a playing position (10 seconds)
Step 60. Adjust the tuning slide (30 seconds)
Step 61. Empty the water key (10 seconds)
Step 62. Inspect the slide for any dents (5 minutes)
Step 63. Calibrate the digital tuner (2 minutes)
Step 64. Register for an online music theory course (30 minutes)
Step 65. Lubricate the rotary valve if applicable (5 minutes)
Step 66. Learn about the importance of embouchure (1 hour)
Step 67. Remove the slide protector tip (10 seconds)
Step 68. Practice moving the slide without gripping too hard (15 minutes)
Step 69. Put on some comfortable clothes for practice (5 minutes)
Step 70. Play your very first note (5 seconds)
Step 71. Read about proper instrument storage (20 minutes)
Step 72. Take the instrument out of the shipping box (5 minutes)
Step 73. Buy a trombone floor stand (25 minutes)
Step 74. Enroll in a "Music 101" webinar (2 hours)
Step 75. Purchase a mute for quiet practice (20 minutes)
Step 76. Mark the tempo on a piece of music (1 minute)
Step 77. Practice the slide transition for G (10 minutes)
Step 78. Learn how to read a rhythm staff (30 minutes)
Step 79. Organize your music folders (20 minutes)
Step 80. Reflect on your progress (10 minutes)
